correctness.rationale: Pairwise bin-union measures give the exact finite covariance. Its positive binomial expansion proves sign, strictness and unique half-bin minimization; two orthogonal binary partitions prove exact independence at two bins. Poissonized independent cell processes give a one-dependent multivariate CLT, and sequential-addition martingale de-Poissonization supplies the fixed-sample correction. Exact phase integration and Fourier transform give the remaining formulas. The standalone checker passed 325 rational-enumeration and analytic checks. No functional limit or unverified numerical-to-infinite inference is asserted.

originality.rationale: The closest primary works cover averaged linear histogram density estimation and fixed-partition occupancy-frequency CLTs, but do not state the nonempty-bin phase cross covariance, all-size strict positivity boundary, exceptional exact independence or Gaussian phase kernel. Statement-level comparisons were performed; broader occupancy-field or overlap theorems remain a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed older finite random-set overlap formulas might recover the explicit covariance as a specialization.
A broad correlated-occupancy Gaussian-field theorem may imply the finite-dimensional CLT, though the explicit kernel and strict finite classification still need comparison.
A separately published 2026 record about multinomial histogram roughness was available only as a summary; it has a distinct observable but was not inspected in full.

value.rationale: Phase choices create observable differences in category-coverage and bin-representation statistics. The exact all-size half-grid minimization, the sharp boundary between genuine dependence and two-bin independence, the multi-phase Gaussian uncertainty kernel and its strictly positive spectrum give meaningful calibration beyond one-bin occupancy. The deterministic spacing representation and exact phase-integrated variance support origin-robust histogram coverage summaries; no unsupported general density-estimation performance theorem is asserted.
